author: SWERY_51
quote:
The level design (metroidvania mecanics, map, traps, secrets), cinematics staging (especially before each boss) and art style are really nice. However, I am disapointed with the gameplay (input lag, annoying whip/hook mecanic that constanly needs an input direction to work properly, a dodge/dash with no I-frame - fortunately you unlock a parry later on) and with the musics that are repetitive. Musics were great in The Rogue Prince of Persia because levels were shors, here, you can explore the same level for an hour long or more, so the short music loop can be tiresome. Also, temporary check points would have been a nice addition, as mirror save points are scattered. The teleportation mechanics is a nightmare, you are punished with a double loading screen each time, and as if that weren't annoying enough, some mirros are broken on purpose and cannot be used.
In the end, it is a great Metroidvania, that you will definitely enjoy if you liked games like Prince of Persia The Lost Crown and Dead Cells. But if you're looking for something similar to the oldest Castlevania entries, like Symphony of the Night, then you might be disapointed.

author: SWERY_51
quote:
When Twin Peaks meets Silent Hill in a 2D Horror-vania adventure.
The atmophere is incredible, the gameplay is great, mixing firearms/hand-to-hand combat and exploration with nice puzzles/investigation. The progression is really addictive and rewarding with a substantial map and with everything needed to make a good metroidvania. Story is intriguing and visuals are top notch. My only grip is the slightly jerky feeling while moving around the environnment (on PS5), but nothing too serious. It took me 20 hours to get the Platinum Trophy (still stuck at 99% completion tho?). Without a doubt GOTY contender if you like the genre.

Absolute Cinema!

My only two grips with the game right now are, the very slow start (i am okay with it, but people need to know that it could takes few hours before really get started), and the technical issues (the framerate is taking a hit on some area especially when there are a lot of ennemies on the map, even on PS5 Pro). Otherwise, everything else is beyond expectation. Gameplay mechanics, level design, atmosphere, writting, music, visuals, sound effects, lightening, Remedyverse, etc. are top notch. The game also do not take you fully by the hand, which is great. It is a perfect example of why I love video games so much.

You fight rivals on a unique map (Tokyo ring road by night), win money (XP), upgrade your cars, buy new ones, unlock new skills (there are different skill trees) to become stronger and be able to defeat more powerful rivals, like in a classic RPG. Simple but really satisfying, and it is running pretty smoothly on PS5 Pro. The only downsides I found are, there is no cockpit view, the translation is awfull (even if it is not important for this kind of game) and the price point is a little high, 35-40€ would have been more appropriate IMO.

author: SWERY_51
quote:
Dead Island 2 is everything i was hoping for. A fun, technically solid, and immersive experience which fully respect the first game. Dambuster Studios nailed it pretty well.

Pros :
+ Good graphics (especially the lighting)
+ Runs pretty well on PS5 (1800p at 60fps, can also adjust motion blur and FOV)
+ Fun gameplay, with a lot of different customizable weapons and skills to unlock
+ You can actually play with physics (water + electricity for example) and set traps
+ Nice level design with shortcuts to unlock and rewarding exploration
+ I've completed the main story in 25 hours (solo) with only 45% of total completion
+ Zombies have a lot of different skins that are changing depending the area you are
+ Very, very gory (Flesh system thing is a blast)

Cons :
- You cannot close doors behind you while exploring
- Storage locker is way too small (only 16 slots!?)
- Low replay value (no new game plus mode yet)
- Needs a photo mode

Pros :
+ Interesting dark story with great characters
+ Neat graphic style
+ Nice soundtrack
+ No annoying calendar "à la" Persona
+ Good length, not too short, not too long
+ Choice between Japanese and English voices (+ several language subtitles choices)
+ Some cool options, like the possibility to adjust the distance of the camera
+ You can save your progression at any time
+ Great classic JRPG turn based combat system with few new features
+ 4 different difficulty settings (the game is quite easy, so do not hesitate to select Hard or Very Hard)

Cons :
- Not very original in the end
- Dungeons design could have been better
- Few quests are only available in NG+, which means you can't achieve 100% in 1 playthrough
- Irritating and annoying costly DLCs (with exclusive Personae and a new story chapter...)

author: SWERY_51
quote:
Persona is an amazing Jrpg series, but not for everyone. So let's recap important things that can help you to decide if you should play Persona 5 (Royal) or not.

- First, there are a lots, lots of cut-scenes and dialogues, so if you're the kind of player that generally skip those because you find it boring, the game is not for you
- You are not free to do whatever you want whenever you want, there is a calendar and schedules to respect, it is not like The Witcher 3 for example
- Combats are turn based like in old school RPGs
- It takes place in Japan, and you are playing as a japanese student
- Game length is pretty long (120 to 150 hours for this Royal edition) with a very slow paced that you can't really rush because of the calendar aspect
- Personae can reminds Pokemons (in a more complex way), as you can collect them and level up them to unlock new abilities, they also have the system of strenghts and weaknesses to various types of element
- The game often introduce serious matters like abuse, suicide and more, it is not for children despite it's colorful anime graphic style
- It is difficult to have an opinion based only on the few first hours as the tutorial is very long and new game mechanics can appears even after 25 hours of gameplay
- Unlike Shin Megami Tensei and other Persona games, this one is very casual friendly, so you don't need to worry about the difficulty even if you're not used to play turn based RPGs, there are 5 different difficulty settings which should satisfied most of the players
- To roughly sum it up, Persona 5 is a mix between Pokemon and a visual novel (but don't take that too seriously, because i'm myself not a huge fan of Pokemon or visual novels, however i love Persona)

If you're cool with everything i just listed above, you should probably give a try to Persona 5, it is a wonderful Jrpg (probably the best one of this generation) that will keep you busy for a long, long time.

The RPG elements are more present than ever, weapons can now level up, you can still choose between 4 classes and replay the missions at higher difficulties to loot new weapons and upgrade your armor. Some things have been improved, like the loadings between missions which are very short now, or enemies that are leaving huge blood splatters and now have visual damage effects and dismemberment. Graphics are close to EDF 4.1, so it stills looking dated, but that's not a problem with this kind of game IMO. There are plenty of missions and the game seems to be very, very long. There is an on-line mode (you will have to redo missions from scratch as its separated from solo mode, but you will keep the upgrades and weapons you already have from solo or the ones you will earn on-line and vice versa) and you can also do split-screen 2 players coop.

It is easily one of the best entry in the series, HOWEVER, i am very disappointed with the technical part. The screen tearing is very annoying (no V-Sync) on any outside mission, and the frame-rate is not flawless. For an episode exclusive to the PS4, this aspect is kind of a let down, be warned. I'm not even hoping for an update here, since the game is available in Japan since a few months, i doubt it will ever be improved with a patch in a near future.

In short, if you enjoyed previous games, and if the technical issues mentioned are not a problem for you, you can pick this one without hesitation.

quote:
Obviously not design for anyone, but if you are a Versus Fighting game lover, it's a blast. Graphics are pretty decent even if the animations looks a little dull. It's very fun to play and the on-line network seems to work fine. Finally, you can select classic SFEX's musics in the option menu, which is amazing.

Note that there is no solo mode. Only a 2 players local versus mode, a training mode (in which you can fight against AI) and a challenge mode to learn combos. The rest is classic on-line modes.

Content: 12 playable characters (13 in standard edition) and 5 stages (each one available in two versions) + the training stage.

I just regret i can't fight AI in the Off-line Versus mode, because training mode just let you play in the training stage.

If you are just a casual gamer looking for solo content, it's not meant for you.
If you are an old school fighting game player, missing the good old time with your friends on games like Street Fighter EX , then it's an absolute must have!

author: SWERY_51
quote:
What is Neon Chrome ?

First of all, a twin sticks shooter with a retro cyber punk design that reminds me D-Generation for example, which is kind of cool.

Then it's a rogue-like who takes the mechanics of Rogue Legacy. You can upgrade several stats with money (health, attack, "mana", luck...) that will be kept for your next character when you die. Every time you star a run, you can choose between 3 characters with differents abilities and weapons, the Assassin is invisible in dark places, the Hacker can pirate some chests and computers...

There are 5 floor to explore, each floor possesses more levels to explore with more rewards and more challenge, and at the end of each you will find a boss. If you beat it, you will open a shortcut to the next floor that you can use freely in your next runs.

Of course every level is randomly generated and feels quite different every time (except for the bosses). There is a lots of secrets to find, new weapons, new perks and stuff. It's smooth and addictive and the soundtrack is fine.

To make it short, you take a twin stick shooter like Alienation, you mix it with the mechanics of Rogue Legacy and with an 80's Blade Runner stylish design, and you will get Neon Chrome.

quote: Biggest disappointement ever. It was supposed to be a great game, with a lot of content, lot of things to do, lots of planets to explore... It just look like a f**king demo! Do NOT put 50$ in that, it is not worth it at all. There are only 3 goods points, the gameplay is fine, the graphics are nice and the musics pretty good. That's it, it is not a MMO, main quest can only be done with 2 other players and the socail aspect ****, it is not an adventure game either (forget everything you heard about Mass Effect, because it's not), it is just a boring FPS, far from Halo or Borderlands. What a waste.
